reason: This passage (1 Samuel 1) depicts the birth narrative of Samuel and focuses on Hannah's barrenness, her prayer, and her dedication of her son to the Lord. While there is interpersonal conflict—Peninnah vexing Hannah out of jealousy—this is rivalry between co-wives, not antagonism of regular people toward a leader. The relationships with authority figures (Elkanah and Eli the priest) show respect and cooperation. When Eli misinterprets Hannah's silent prayer as drunkenness and rebukes her, Hannah politely clarifies without antagonism, and Eli responds with blessing. There is no depiction of the general people being antagonistic toward their leader.
